B
Probability is a measure of the likelihood of an event. A fair coin has two equally likely outcomes (heads or tails), so the probability of getting heads is 1 out of 2, or 50%.

C
The events are independent because the result of the die roll has no influence on the result of the coin flip, and vice versa.

B
Conditional probability is used because the probability of the second event (drawing a red ball) is dependent on the outcome of the first event (drawing a blue ball), which has already occurred and changed the conditions.

B
Bayes' theorem is used to update the probability for a hypothesis as more evidence becomes available. It mathematically relates a conditional probability to its inverse, allowing us to find P(A|B) by using P(B|A), which is essential for updating beliefs.

B
This statement is the mathematical definition of independence. If two events are independent, the occurrence of one event does not provide any information about the probability of the other event, so the conditional probability P(A|B) is equal to the regular (marginal) probability P(A).
